key_insight: Proxy3D compresses multi-view visual information into compact, semantically meaningful 3D proxies and aligns them with language, achieving spatially consistent 3D representations for VLMs with much lower compute and memory than dense correspondence or volumetric methods.
problem_solved: Existing VLM approaches either use expensive dense 3D priors or brittle pixel-aligned correspondence and therefore fail to provide efficient, spatially consistent 3D understanding for vision-language tasks.
method: Semantic clustering: aggregate multi-view features into a small set of 3D semantic proxies (clusters) that summarize scene geometry and semantics.
Cross-modal alignment: align proxy embeddings with language tokens using contrastive and alignment losses so proxies become language-aware 3D anchors.
Lightweight indexing & retrieval: use the compact proxies at inference for fast spatial queries and reasoning instead of operating on dense 3D volumes or per-pixel correspondences.
impact: Provides a practical, efficient way to add true 3D spatial reasoning to vision-language models, reducing compute/memory and improving spatial consistency — useful for robotics, AR, and multi-view VLM applications.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: multi-view images → feature extraction → semantic clustering → proxy set → alignment with text (shows data reduction and flow).
Before/after comparison: dense pixel-aligned map vs. compact Proxy3D clusters, annotated with memory and latency savings.
Bar chart: metrics comparing accuracy, inference time, and memory of Proxy3D vs. correspondence-based and volumetric baselines.
Qualitative scene examples: 3D scene with proxies and language queries showing correct spatial answers (e.g., 'Where is the red cup?').
paper_title: Proxy3D: Efficient 3D Representations for Vision-Language Models via Semantic Clustering and Alignment
paper_authors: Jerry Jiang, Haowen Sun, Denis Gudovskiy, Yohei Nakata, Tomoyuki Okuno
